name: Jollof Rice
blurb: The beloved party rice of Nigeria and Ghana — smoky, tomato-rich, and always at the centre of celebrations, Sundays, and friendly debates about who makes it best.

ingredients.name: Long-grain parboiled rice
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less smoky absorption; grains break more easily — still tasty.

ingredients.name: Fresh tomatoes
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Slightly less fresh sweetness; add a pinch of sugar.

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers
ingredients.substitution: Tatashe if you can find it
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Tatashe gives the classic colour and mild heat.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet
ingredients.substitution: Habanero or ½ tsp chilli flakes
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Similar heat; habanero is a touch fruitier.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Loses some depth; paprika brings back smokiness. Makes it vegetarian.

steps.text: Blend tomatoes, bell peppers, scotch bonnet and half an onion until smooth.
Fry sliced onion and tomato paste in oil until the paste darkens and tastes sweet.
steps.why: Frying off the raw edge of tomato paste is what gives party-style depth.

steps.text: Add the blended mix and simmer until thick and the oil rises to the top.
steps.why: Thickening now means fluffy, separate grains later — watery sauce makes soggy rice.

steps.text: Stir in stock, thyme, bay leaf and salt. Bring to a boil, then add rinsed rice.
Cover tightly with foil + lid and cook on low until rice is tender.
steps.why: Trapped steam does the cooking — resist peeking for the first 15 minutes.

name: Egusi Soup
blurb: A hearty melon-seed soup eaten across Nigeria — nutty, rich, and made for scooping with swallow. A Sunday staple in many homes.

ingredients.name: Ground egusi (melon seeds)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Close in texture; slightly milder and less nutty.

ingredients.name: Palm oil
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Loses the signature colour and earthy flavour — honest downgrade.

ingredients.name: Smoked mackerel
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Mushrooms keep it savoury but lose the smoky-fish depth.

steps.text: Mix ground egusi with a splash of water into a thick paste; set aside.
Heat palm oil, fry onion, then add stock and bring to a simmer.
Scoop in egusi paste in lumps and simmer without stirring.
steps.why: Leaving it alone lets the egusi set into lovely crumbs instead of mush.

steps.text: Stir gently, add fish, greens and seasoning. Simmer until greens are tender.

name: Fufu
blurb: Soft, stretchy swallow pounded from cassava and plantain — the scoop you use for soups like egusi and groundnut stew. Eaten daily across Ghana, Nigeria and beyond.

ingredients.name: Cassava flour (or fufu flour)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less stretch, much easier — a fair trade on busy days.

steps.text: Bring water to a boil, then whisk in the flour a little at a time.
Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until smooth and stretchy.
steps.why: Elbow grease now is what gives fufu its pull — keep turning, don't stop.

steps.text: Wet your hands, shape into balls and serve warm with soup.

name: Waakye
blurb: Ghana's famous rice-and-beans, cooked with sorghum leaves for its brick-red colour. A classic street breakfast wrapped in banana leaves with all the extras.

ingredients.name: Black-eyed beans
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Softer; skip the pre-boil and shorten cooking by ~20 min.

ingredients.name: Dried sorghum (waakye) leaves
ingredients.substitution: 1 tsp baking soda for colour only
ingredients.substitutionImpact: You get a brownish tint, not the classic red — flavour mostly unchanged.

steps.text: Boil beans with sorghum leaves until almost tender.
Remove leaves, add rice, salt and water. Cover and cook on low.
steps.why: Beans need a head start or the rice turns to mush before they soften.

steps.text: Rest 10 minutes, fluff, and serve with extras (egg, shito, spaghetti).

name: Puff-Puff
blurb: Golden, pillowy fried dough balls — the snack of every Nigerian party and street corner. Best eaten warm, standing up, with friends.

ingredients.name: Ground nutmeg
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Less traditional warmth; still sweet and lovely.

steps.text: Mix everything into a thick batter. Cover and proof until doubled and bubbly.
steps.why: A full, bubbly rise is what makes them hollow-light instead of dense.

steps.text: Heat oil to 170–175°C. Scoop batter with oiled hands or a spoon.
Fry in batches, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on paper.
steps.why: Crowding the pot drops the oil temperature and makes them greasy.

name: Groundnut Stew
blurb: Known as mafé across Senegal and Mali — a comforting peanut stew, gently sweet and savoury, eaten with rice or fufu on family evenings.

ingredients.name: Natural peanut butter (no sugar)
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Grainier texture, deeper roast flavour — very good.

ingredients.name: Chicken pieces
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Lighter but still hearty; add an extra spoon of peanut butter.

ingredients.name: Carrots & sweet potato
ingredients.substitutionImpact: Sweeter and softer — lovely, just watch the simmer time.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in oil; set aside.
Fry onion and tomato paste, then whisk in stock and peanut butter until smooth.
steps.why: Whisking bit by bit stops the peanut splitting later.

steps.text: Return chicken plus vegetables. Simmer until tender and oil glistens on top.
